# /mod-compact — Keep the records small

**Requires agent: `Guide`.** Under another agent, stop and ask the developer to switch.

`docs/` only grows. Every focused analysis adds a note, every rework or fix adds to a step's
status, decisions pile up, and the plans of a component that's already live keep every
walk-through, coverage ledger and build step that got it there. Every command reads parts of
`docs/`, so what's past costs tokens on every run and crowds out what matters now. Compacting
condenses, in place, the detail that's **settled** (past, superseded or finished), keeps
everything still in use word for word, and **changes nothing until a backup of `docs/` is
verified.**

It never:
- deletes, renames or moves a file under `docs/`: code comments and links cite plan files by
  path;
- removes an ID, a heading, a header field (`**Status:**`, `**Plan:**`…), a `path:line`, an
  exact value or a link target;
- touches work in progress: the plans of a component that isn't built, live or kept, a paused
  step, an OPEN question, or anything that rests on one;
- summarizes a question: settled rows move to the archive word for word, as `/mod-answer
  archive` does;
- edits `legacy/`, `modern/`, `docs/reports/` (regenerated by their commands) or
  `docs/archive/` (word for word);
- changes a file's **Updated:** date: nothing in it changed in substance.

What can be condensed, when, and into what is in [catalog.md](catalog.md).

Values in `<ANGLE BRACKETS>` come from the text after the command.

| Argument | What you do |
|---|---|
| nothing | § 1–6 for all of `docs/` |
| `<component>` | § 1–6 for that component's folder only |
| `improvements` | § 1–6 for `docs/improvements/` only |
| `how` | § 7 When to compact |

## 1. Check (changes nothing)

**a. Each component's tier.** Its stage, by the rules of
[/mod-track § 1](../mod-track/SKILL.md#1-stages-and-next-actions), decides how much of its
folder may be condensed:

| Tier | Stage | What may be condensed |
|---|---|---|
| **active** | found, analysed, planning, ready to build, building, paused, blocked, or in need of attention | only the lines of `component.md § Notes` that repeat what's recorded elsewhere |
| **built** | built (every item done, the tests pass), not live yet | as active, and the history in its plans: rework and fix histories on done steps, complete coverage ledgers |
| **live** | live, or kept | the whole catalog |

A built component may still get fixes while old and new run side by side, so its plans keep
their detail until it's live. When the records don't settle a stage, take the earlier one.

**b. Measure.** Lines per file, and per section of each file that may hold something to
condense. With more than about 15 components, don't open every file: send Scout briefs over
`docs/components/` (at most 3 in parallel), for example:

```text
GOAL:     measure the records of <components> for compaction
WHERE:    docs/components/<component>/ (docs/, read-only: this skill's brief allows it)
LOOK FOR: each file's lines; each ## section's lines; dated § Notes entries
          (^- \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}); statuses with more than one "reworked (" or "fixed (";
          the **Compacted:** field and its date
RETURN:   File | Lines | Sections (lines each) | Notes entries | Status histories | Compacted
LIMIT:    40 files; stop and list what's left
```

Then read whole only the sections that may qualify.

**c. Apply the catalog** to each section: whether it's settled for the tier, and its compacted
form. A file compacted before (its **Compacted:** field) is condensed only for what was added
after that date: compacted text is never condensed again, so nothing drifts further from the
original with each run.

**d. The question bank.** Run the check of
[/mod-answer § 5a](../mod-answer/SKILL.md#a-check-changes-nothing). The rows that can move
join this run, under the same backup, and move word for word as its
[§ 5c](../mod-answer/SKILL.md#c-archive) says.

**When you're unsure** whether something is settled, or whether something cites it, it stays.

## 2. The proposal

Show, in chat:
- **`docs/` now:** files and lines in all, by folder, and the 10 largest files;
- **what can be condensed,** one row per file:

  | File | Tier | Sections | How (catalog) | Lines before → after |
  |---|---|---|---|---|

- **the question bank:** the rows that can move, and its lines after, or "nothing to archive";
- **what stays, and why:** the active components with their stage, and anything left because
  it's still in use;
- **the total:** lines before → after, and the share saved;
- **a preview** of the largest change: that section before and after, at most 25 lines;
- **the backups** already in `.backup/` (file search), oldest first.

Nothing qualifies: say so, name what would settle something next ("orders-core goes live"),
and stop. Otherwise ask with `askQuestions` (header "Compact"): ★ **Back up, then compact** ·
**Only some** (the developer names the files or components: show the new totals and ask
again) · **Not now**. Without the tool, number the options and stop.

## 3. Back up `docs/` (before anything changes)

The whole of `docs/` goes to a backup folder first, so the full text of everything you condense
stays at hand. It's a copy, not a move: `docs/` stays whole should the run stop halfway, and
the files you don't condense aren't rewritten. You never run commands, so the developer makes
it, in one command. Name it `docs-YYYY-MM-DD` (today), with `-2`, `-3`… when that folder
already exists (file search in `.backup/`), and show it in a copy-ready block:

```powershell
Set-Location "<workspace>"; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .backup | Out-Null; Copy-Item -Path docs -Destination ".backup/docs-YYYY-MM-DD" -Recurse
```

Then ask (header "Backup"): ★ **Done, check it** · **Cancel**. Verify before going on: the
folder exists, it holds as many files as `docs/` (file search on both), and every file the
proposal changes is there with as many lines as the live one. Anything off: say what, and ask
again. **Never compact without a verified backup.**

`.backup/` is outside `docs/` and out of git (`.gitignore`), and shared with `/mod-answer
archive`. No other command reads or searches it; this one reads it only to verify and restore.

## 4. Compact, one file at a time

For each file in the accepted proposal, in turn:
1. **Note before:** every ID in it (as
   [catalog.md § Always stays](catalog.md#always-stays) lists them), every heading, and every
   link target.
2. **Condense** the sections in the proposal, as the catalog says. Edit only those sections;
   never rewrite a whole file.
3. **Mark it:** add `· **Compacted:** YYYY-MM-DD (full text: .backup/docs-YYYY-MM-DD)` after
   the last field of the file's header line (the `**…:**` fields under its title; in
   `modern.md` and `system.md`, whose header runs on into prose, right after **Updated:**). A
   file compacted before: change that field's date and folder.
4. **Verify** it (§ 5) before the next file.

Then the question rows, as [/mod-answer § 5c](../mod-answer/SKILL.md#c-archive) says.

## 5. Verify, and restore if anything's off

After each file:
- every ID, heading and link target noted before is still there, and an ID whose row is in
  this file is there exactly once;
- every link in the file still resolves;
- it has no more lines than before;
- what always stays is unchanged: compare each row you shortened with the backup, character
  for character, in the cells the catalog keeps word for word (exact details, expected values,
  messages, recorded legacy outputs, `path:line`).

After the last file:
- every ID and `docs/…` path cited in `modern/` (a read-only search for the ID patterns, for
  `docs/components/`, `docs/improvements/` and `Decision YYYY-MM-DD`) still resolves: the ID
  in `docs/` or in `docs/archive/questions.md`, the path as a file;
- the question bank, as
  [/mod-answer § 5d](../mod-answer/SKILL.md#d-verify-and-restore-if-anythings-off) says.

Anything off: say what failed, and restore that file from the backup (VS Code's Undo on this
chat's edits of it, or this command for the developer), then stop. The files already compacted
and verified stay as they are.

```powershell
Set-Location "<workspace>"; Copy-Item ".backup/docs-YYYY-MM-DD/<path under docs>" "docs/<path under docs>" -Force
```

## 6. Report

In chat:
- each file: lines before → after, and the sections condensed; the question rows moved;
- the total: `docs/` lines before → after, and the share saved;
- the backup's path, and how to restore one file (§ 5) or all of `docs/`, should it ever be
  needed:

```powershell
Set-Location "<workspace>"; Copy-Item -Path ".backup/docs-YYYY-MM-DD/*" -Destination docs -Recurse -Force
```

Then: "Commit `docs/` now: git history then holds both the full and the compacted versions."
Old backups are the developer's to delete: suggest keeping the last 3. End with the next
action, as [/mod-track § 4](../mod-track/SKILL.md#4-next) gives it.

## 7. When to compact

When the developer asks (`how`):
1. When `/mod-track` says the records need compacting.
2. After a component goes live, or is kept: its plans are settled.
3. After a wave is done, or when the question bank needs archiving: one backup covers both.
4. Compacting twice in a row condenses nothing the second time; between runs, only what was
   added since a file's **Compacted:** date is condensed.

The full text is never lost: it's in the backup, and in git history once `docs/` is committed.

## Unknowns

`/mod-compact` reads the records and finds nothing new about the legacy system, so it logs no
questions. When the records can't tell, the text stays as it is:

| Can't tell | What happens |
|---|---|
| a component's stage | the earlier stage the records support, and its tier |
| whether a decision is superseded | it stays word for word |
| whether a note's finding is recorded elsewhere | it stays |
| whether code, a plan or a command cites a section | it stays |
| whether a status history has an open re-check | it stays |
